Figure 1. This figure illustrates the overall framework of our CoA-VLA model, which empowers vision-language-action models with
chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities for generalizable visuomotor policy learning. We achieve this by designing four distinct types of
affordance and introducing a novel visual-text co-injection method to integrate this knowledge into the decision-making process.

                                                                           Explicit reasoning is essential for language models to han-
Figure 5. Movement generalization for CoA-VLA. CoA-                        dle complex tasks. In this work, we design a reasoning-
VLA can avoid obstacles and operate safely.                                aware foundation model for robotics, focusing on various
                                                                           affordances: object, grasp, spatial, and movement. These
                                                                           affordances form an interdependent chain: the robot iden-
robot is presented with a plate on which three distinct ob-                tifies the target object and location, determines how to
jects are already placed, and it is instructed to add a piece              grasp it, decides where to place it, and navigates accord-
of bread onto the plate. Our method successfully identifies                ingly. By structuring this chain of affordances as interme-
open areas on the plate, allowing it to accurately position the            diate language and image outputs and feeding this reason-
bread without interference, thereby enabling CoA-VLA to                    ing into the policy model, our Chain-of-Affordances (CoA-
complete all three task scenarios with precision. In con-                  VLA) model outperforms baselines on real-world robotic
trast, alternative methods, such as OpenVLA and Diffusion-                 tasks.CoA-VLA models also generalize well to complex en-
VLA, succeed in only one scenario each, failing to general-                vironments, tackling challenges like grasping in unfamiliar
ize across all spatial configurations. This experiment under-              orientations, avoiding obstacles, and spatial generalization.
scores the crucial role of spatial affordance in enhancing the             Our approach provides a novel perspective on designing
model’s ability to recognize and utilize available space, ul-              reasoning chains to enhance embodied control.
timately improving task completion accuracy and reliability
across varied setups.
